inventedEvidence.evidence: "Thanks for letting us know about the lint filter status" - customer had only said "I haven't cleaned it yet"; assistant also proceeded as though the filter check was done, and framed the fault as overheating/cut-out which the customer explicitly denied ("it doesnt break down")

confidentUnsupported.evidence: "A blocked filter makes the dryer overheat, and it then cuts out to protect itself" - asserted as the cause despite the customer stating the dryer dries fine and the only issue is the drum turning after 'End'

blockingLoop.evidence: "Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?" asked twice verbatim, then re-asked for the condenser, while the customer twice asked "is that really why it keeps turning after End?" without an answer

rationale: The customer clearly described the classic anti-crease behaviour (drum turns intermittently after 'End', dries fine, no fault), yet the assistant ignored this entirely and ran a canned overheating/cut-out script about blocked filters and condensers. It never acknowledged the actual symptom, never asked the key clarifying questions (does it stop when the door opens, is it heating), and repeated the same filter question twice before moving to a condenser clean, all irrelevant. The customer directly asked twice whether the filter explained the turning and was never answered. Nothing unsafe was advised and no parts were pushed, but the homeowner left with no understanding that this is normal behaviour.
